profile.campus: Clarksville-Montgomery County, Tennessee (Google's Boolean Drive / Jim Johnson Road campus)
profile.address: Boolean Drive, Montgomery County, Middle Tennessee, Tennessee
profile.reading: This building, tagged SPC3A in OpenStreetMap (labeled "Building 3" in the source data), is part of the continued expansion of Google's Clarksville-Montgomery County data center campus beyond the original SPC1A building that opened in November 2019. Google, the Tennessee Valley Authority, and Governor Bill Haslam's administration announced the original roughly $600 million Clarksville project through the Tennessee Department of Economic and Community Development, with construction beginning in February 2018 and the first building opening in a ribbon-cutting ceremony led by then-Governor Bill Lee on November 6, 2019; Google has continued adding buildings to the Boolean Drive campus in the years since as demand for its cloud and AI infrastructure grew. The campus draws power in part through a 413-megawatt renewable energy purchase agreement Google struck with the Tennessee Valley Authority, sourced from solar farms totaling roughly 1.6 million panels across sites in Tennessee and Alabama. Google has said it gave more than $450,000 to local nonprofits and schools in the Clarksville area in the years following the data center's opening. Since construction began in 2018, Google reports investing more than $6 billion in Tennessee overall, a figure that under its updated economic-impact methodology includes data center construction along with server and networking capital expenditure rather than construction costs alone, and the company says it helped generate $11.4 billion of economic activity for Tennessee businesses, nonprofits, and developers in 2025. Google's data center locations page and its economic-impact reporting do not break these totals out per building, so this registry records them as regional context rather than facts specific to the SPC3A building, and treats the Boolean Drive address, drawn from OpenStreetMap's reverse-geocoded coordinates, as the best currently available location detail for this structure pending a county assessor parcel lookup.

reading.body:
Google does not publish power capacity, square footage, or exact addresses for individual buildings at its Clarksville-Montgomery County data center campus, including SPC3A. The regional investment figure for the campus is approximately $600 million, reported by DataCenterDynamics and ClarksvilleNow at the time of Google's official opening, but this translates to no disclosed wattage for this specific building.

Tennessee has 24 mapped data center facilities. Only four facilities in the state have published power figures from operator spec pages, totaling 12.13 MW. SPC3A ranks fifth in the state by published capacity, which means it has no published figure and is ranked behind the four facilities with disclosed specs.

Without published power capacity for this building, its relevance to AI scaling cannot be assessed from available data. Google's disclosure policy treats individual facility specifications as confidential, making this site's ability to measure the campus's contribution to state or regional AI infrastructure dependent on future operator transparency or independent verification methods.
